## Overview

`ctasapp` is a Shiny application for exploring results from the
[ctas](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctas) (Clinical Timeseries
Anomaly Spotter) R package. Input data and site scores are produced with
[gsm.ctas](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas), which wraps ctas
in mapping, metric and reporting workflows:

```
Raw SDTM domains (dm, lb, vs, eg, rs, queries, pd)
  |
  v
gsm.ctas mapping workflows     -- Standardize_Domain() + Transform_*()
  |
  v
gsm.ctas metric workflows      -- ctas site-level outlier scores
  |
  v
gsm.ctas reporting workflows   -- Write_ctasapp() writes upload files
  |
  v
ctasapp (Shiny visualization)  -- interactive exploration of scores, plots, and data
```


## Input data structure

The **Input** upload file has one row per subject/timepoint/parameter:

| Column | Type | Description |
|:-------|:-----|:------------|
| `subject_id` | character | Subject identifier (USUBJID) |
| `site` | character | Site identifier |
| `parameter_id` | character | Unique parameter key (e.g. `RANGE_ALT`, `SYSBP`) |
| `parameter_name` | character | Human-readable label |
| `parameter_category_1` | character | Broad domain (e.g. "Labs", "Vital Signs") |
| `parameter_category_2` | character | Field-level grouping key (e.g. "ALT", "SYSBP") |
| `parameter_category_3` | character | Plot type: see table below |
| `timepoint_rank` | integer | Positional visit index (1, 2, 3, ...) |
| `timepoint_1_name` | character | Visit label (e.g. "WEEK 2", "SCREENING 1") |
| `result` | numeric | Transformed value analysed by ctas |

The `parameter_category_3` value determines how the parameter is visualized:

| `parameter_category_3` | Plot type | Produced by (gsm.ctas) |
|:------------------------|:----------|:------------|
| `range_normalized` | Faceted line plot (values in 0--1 range) | `Transform_Range()` |
| `ratio_missing` | Faceted line plot (paired with range_normalized) | `Transform_Missing()` |
| `numeric` | Line plot (raw values) | `Standardize_Domain()` |
| `categorical` | Alluvial / stacked bar plot | `Transform_OneHot()` |
| `bar` | Single-timepoint bar chart | Inferred for `categorical` fields where the median subject has one timepoint (e.g. `BMICAT`) |

Parameters sharing a `parameter_category_2` are shown together as one field.
For example `RANGE_ALT` (range-normalized) and `MISS_ALT` (running ratio of
missing values) both have `parameter_category_2 = "ALT"` and are displayed as
a faceted pair. Range normalization maps values within the reference range
to 0--1:

$$\text{result} = \frac{\text{value} - \text{lower}}{\text{upper} - \text{lower}}$$


## Generating data with gsm.ctas

The bundled sample data is created by `data-raw/sample_data.R`, which runs
the gsm.ctas workflows on the SDTM data shipped with gsm.ctas:

```{r gsm-ctas-workflow, eval = FALSE}
lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = gsm.ctas::dm, Raw_LB = gsm.ctas::lb, Raw_VS = gsm.ctas::vs,
  Raw_EG = gsm.ctas::eg, Raw_RS = gsm.ctas::rs,
  Raw_Queries = gsm.ctas::queries, Raw_PD = gsm.ctas::pd
)

wf_path <- function(layer) system.file("workflow", layer, package = "gsm.ctas")
lMappingWorkflows   <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = wf_path("1_mappings"))
lMetricWorkflows    <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = wf_path("2_metrics"))
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = wf_path("3_reporting"))

lMapped <- workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows,
  lData = gsm.mapping::Ingest(lRaw, gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows))
)
lAnalysis <- workr::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows, lData = lMapped)
lReporting <- workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows,
  lData = c(lMapped, list(lAnalyzed = lAnalysis,
                          lMetricWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows))
)

# Writes results, input, untransformed, queries and pd as parquet
gsm.ctas::Write_ctasapp(lReporting, "~/my_upload_files")
```


## Example plots

The package bundles the gsm.ctas output as `sample_data` and
`sample_results`. These can be used directly to generate all plot types.

```{r prepare-measures}
m <- prepare_measures(sample_data, sample_results)
```

### Range-normalized lab values with missingness ratio

```{r plot-range-norm, fig.height = 7}
plot_timeseries(c("RANGE_ALT", "MISS_ALT"), m, thresh = 1.3)
```

### Plain numeric vital signs

```{r plot-numeric}
plot_timeseries("SYSBP", m, thresh = 1.3)
```

### Categorical (alluvial)

Overall response (`OVRLRESP`) categories are displayed as an alluvial plot
showing transitions across visits.

```{r plot-categorical, fig.height = 8}
cat_ids <- unique(m$parameter_id[m$parameter_category_2 == "OVRLRESP"])
plot_categorical(cat_ids, m, thresh = 1.3)
```

### Bar (single-timepoint)

BMI categories (`BMICAT`) are recorded once per subject, so the app renders
them as a bar chart.

```{r plot-bar}
bar_ids <- unique(m$parameter_id[m$parameter_category_2 == "BMICAT"])
plot_bar(bar_ids, m, thresh = 1.3)
```


## Uploading your own data

The app supports uploading custom data via 2 mandatory and 3 optional flat
files (CSV, Parquet, or RDA):

| File | Required | Description |
|:-----|:---------|:------------|
| Results | Yes | Site scores with `parameter_id` per `timeseries_id` |
| Input | Yes | One row per subject/timepoint/parameter (see above) |
| Untransformed | No | Original values before transformation (for display in data tables) |
| Queries | No | Clinical query records (overlaid as dots on plots) |
| Protocol Deviations | No | SDTM DV-style deviations linked at site level (Protocol Deviations tab) |

See the collapsible "File format documentation" panel in the app's Data tab
for full column specifications. An optional `study` column in the Input file
enables multi-study filtering in the Fields panel. Protocol deviations link
at site level only — the Protocol Deviations tab shows rows for the sites
currently plotted for the selected field, without any `parameter_id`
filtering.

### Generating example upload files

The gsm.ctas upload files are shipped as parquet in
`system.file("extdata", package = "ctasapp")`. Use `generate_sample_csv()`
to copy them to a directory, as CSV (default) or parquet:

```{r generate-csv, eval = FALSE}
generate_sample_csv("~/my_upload_files")
generate_sample_csv("~/my_upload_files", format = "parquet")
```

This writes `results`, `input`, `untransformed`, `queries`, and `pd` files
into the specified directory.
